The 1st petitioner is stated to be a trader in fruits and vegetables, and the 2nd petitioner, a seller of aquariums.
It is alleged that the said activities are being carried out in an extent of 1.02 Ares in R.S No.30/4A (New 30/190), comprising in Kavumbhagam desom, Thurvangad village, Thalassery Taluk.
It is alleged that the said plot belongs to the 3rd petitioner, who is the sister of the 2 nd petitioner.

The petitioners had applied for the issuance of ID cards, claiming the status of Street Vendors and were issued with temporary cards, as seen from Exts.P5 and P6.
2.

On the basis of a complaint preferred by the 7 th respondent herein, that his property was also encroached upon, the 2nd respondent issued notices, as seen from Ext.P8, requiring the petitioner to show cause as to why the licence should not be cancelled.
It is submitted that the petitioners had given the reply, notwithstanding which, Ext.P15 order was passed, cancelling the license.
Though the said orders were sought to be challenged 2026:KER:4646 WP(C) NO.18321 OF 2023 before the Tribunal for Local Self Government Institutions, the appeal was held to be not maintainable.

The petitioners had also approached the Committee for Redressal of Grievances of Street Vendors,
Kerala State, which passed Ext.P21 order, recording the submission on the part of the Municipality to reconsider the decision, if the petitioners are prepared to obey the concerned laws and Rules and also giving liberty to the petitioners to apply for Street Vending licences and for ID Cards.

sentences.text:
Based on the above submission of the Municipality, the case was closed by the Committee as follows;
"xxx

We direct the R1 Municipality and its authorities to consider the application, if any filed by the petitioners complying the laws, regulation and Rules of the Municipality read with the provisions in the Central Act No.7/2014 after hearing all concerned including the Second Respondent as expeditiously as possible."
3. It is challenging the said order that the writ petition is filed.

4. The Committee had recorded the submission made on behalf of the Municipality, which required the petitioners to prefer 2026:KER:4646 WP(C) NO.18321 OF 2023 applications subject to them complying with the applicable laws.

If the petitioners have not chosen to make an application so far,
they are granted two weeks from today to make an appropriate application as directed in Ext.P12.
The competent among the respondents 1 to 4 shall consider the same with notice to the petitioners and also to the 7th respondent herein and pass appropriate orders, in accordance with law.
Orders shall be passed within two months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
Taking note of the fact that initially there was an interim order, the status quo as on date shall be maintained till orders are passed.
The writ petition is disposed of as above.
